newsitem.title: POLAND: Five Polish brokers seek OECD securities licence.
newsitem.headline: Five Polish brokers seek OECD securities licence.

text.p: Five Polish brokerages have applied to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) for a licence to invest in securities issued in OECD countries, a KPW spokeswoman said.

A new foreign exchange regulation, which came into force on February 4, allows Poles to invest in stocks and debt securities issued in OECD countries through those domestic securities houses that are granted relevant licences.

Beata Stelmach told Reuters three of the applications concerned intermediary services for Polish investors who want to buy foreign securities and two concerned the inclusion of OECD securities in managed portfolios.
"At the moment we have five applications, three of them concerning intermediary services and two concerning portfolio management," she said.
Stelmach said the first licences were likely to be granted in late February or early March, because the KPW first wanted to consult with the Finance Minister and the Polish central bank (NBP).

Mieczyslaw Lazor, sales department director of IB Austria Securities in Warsaw, said the brokerage, which applied for the KPW licence in January, should be ready to start offering new services in three months.
"We will do our best to be able to launch the services in three months time," he told Reuters.
Lazor said Polish investors seemed moderately interested in the new services.
